pitṛ-ṛṇa.description: The debt owed to one's ancestors or father.

deva-ṛṇa.description: The debt owed to the gods.

sootaka.description: A period of ritual impurity following a death or birth in the family.

janivara.description: The sacred thread worn by Brahmin men after their initiation.

prarabdha karma.description: The portion of past karma that is responsible for one's present life and circumstances.

akshate.description: Unbroken rice grains used in rituals for blessings.

ratha.description: A chariot, especially one used in temple festivals.

parimanchane.description: The ritual seating arrangement for meals or ceremonies.

kosambari.description: A South Indian salad made of lentils and vegetables, often served at feasts.

huLi.description: A sour curry or sambar, a staple in South Indian meals.

laddu.description: A round sweet made from flour, sugar, and ghee.

huli anna.description: Rice mixed with sour curry, a common dish in Karnataka.

madi-Brahmins.description: Brahmins who maintain ritual purity, especially in matters of food and dress.

beedi.description: A thin Indian cigarette filled with tobacco and wrapped in a tendu leaf.

tambula.description: A betel leaf preparation chewed after meals, often with areca nut and lime.

mandi-pet.description: A market area, especially in towns or cities.

choultry.description: A public rest house or inn, often used by pilgrims.

bhikshukas.description: Mendicants or those who beg for alms, often Brahmins in ritual contexts.

jerisalle.description: A type of shawl or cloth, often silk-bordered, worn by Brahmins.

chiroti.description: A layered, flaky sweet pastry from Karnataka.

kamandala.description: A water pot carried by ascetics and sages.
